The Committee’s “patient” pause with inflation below 2 percent and slowing activity is consistent with an estimated policy rule in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler–type frameworks, which prescribe holding or easing when the output gap narrows and realized/expected inflation run below target. The emphasis on anchored longer-term expectations and “muted” price pressures aligns with a flatter New Keynesian Phillips curve and the primacy of expectations in inflation targeting (Svensson and Woodford), helping explain low inflation despite tight labor markets. Citing “global economic and financial developments” reflects awareness of financial accelerator mechanisms (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist), where external shocks can amplify through credit spreads—supporting a cautious stance to stabilize conditions. Low market-based inflation compensation and a flatter yield curve are consistent with macro term-structure evidence (Ang–Piazzesi; Rudebusch–Wu) that long rates embed expectations of a shallower policy path. Operationally, holding IOER at 2.40 percent and continuing balance-sheet reinvestments fit modern operating frameworks for implementing policy via reserves and administered rates (Goodfriend, 2002). Net tone: balanced but dovish relative to January, acknowledging softer growth and subdued inflation while still expecting expansion—slightly less positive than a pure “expansion” message.
